issues.issue: The unqualified promise to advance "your portion of the arbitration expenses" on request conflicts with paragraph 4, which limits any such advance to "up to $1000."

The sentence first makes each party bear its own attorneys' fees and expenses and then preserves "any party's ability to recover costs and attorneys' fees to the extent authorized by law," leaving the fee rule self-cancelling.
The venue guarantee of the customer's county is undone by "or in such other place as shall be ordered by the arbitrator," which is subject to no stated limit.

Forbidding the arbitrator to apply any rules of civil procedure sits awkwardly with the preceding sentence authorising motions "substantially similar to a motion to dismiss for failure to state a claim or a motion for summary judgment," which are creatures of those rules.
"[A] decision or an award in your favor resolving the dispute" does not say whether partial or mixed relief counts, so the fee consequence turns on an undefined outcome.

Mandatory reimbursement by an unsuccessful customer is hard to square with paragraph 4, which leaves it to "the arbitrator [to] decide whether we, Lender, or you ... will ultimately be responsible to pay those fees."

The retained small claims right must be reconciled with paragraph 4, under which "any dispute shall be resolved by binding arbitration" upon election by either side, and with paragraph 2(b)'s waiver of any court other than a small claims tribunal.

"[C]annot be adjudicated within the jurisdiction of a small claims tribunal" does not say whether the test is the amount claimed, the relief sought or the type of claim, leaving the boundary of the carve-out uncertain.

Routing any appeal from a small claims judgment into binding arbitration is in tension with the preceding sentence retaining the small claims forum, since in Texas such an appeal is a trial de novo in the county court.
The Arbitration Provision is made to benefit "related third parties," a class defined only by an inclusive list in paragraph 1(g), so which non-signatories may enforce it is open.

This poison-pill severability rule — invalidity of the class-arbitration waiver voids the entire Arbitration Provision — cannot be squared with the Entire Agreement clause, under which an invalid provision "shall be reformed if practicable" and "shall not in any way affect the remaining provisions."

The opt-out sentence is garbled and the address is given twice in corrupted form ("PL. Juan Store of Texas, Inc., Attn: Arbitration Opt-Ou"), so the place to which notice must be sent is not cleanly stated.

The carve-out making the Arbitration Provision governed by the FAA must be read with paragraph 7, which substitutes Texas arbitration law if a court finds the FAA inapplicable, and with the Texas-law rule for the rest of the Agreement.

The integration clause claims this is the entire agreement "relating to the subject matter," yet the document itself contemplates a separate "Jury Trial Waiver and Arbitration Agreement," a separate lender loan contract and the attached cancellation notices.

This reformation-and-survival rule contradicts paragraph 8 of the Arbitration Provision, under which invalidity of the class-arbitration waiver renders "this entire Arbitration Provision ... void" rather than being reformed or severed.
The list of documents acknowledged as received is broken and incomplete — "(1) A SEPARATE If T; 2) THIS ZES AGREEMENT" — so what the customer is certifying receipt of cannot be read off the clause.

The certification that the customer agrees to "the binding Waiver Of Jury Trial And Arbitration Provision" is difficult to square with the Opt-Out Process, which allows rejection of that provision within 90 days of the same signing.

The warranty of no intention to file for bankruptcy sits against paragraph 8 of the Arbitration Provision, which expressly contemplates that the customer's obligations may be "discharged through bankruptcy."
"[L]egitimate, open, and active" is undefined and the warranty fixes no point in time at which the account must have that character, though the whole consequence of a returned item turns on it.

This account warranty interacts directly with the Collection Expenses paragraph barring criminal charges over a check given as security "in the absence of forgery, fraud, theft, or other criminal conduct," since breach of the warranty is what would be said to supply that conduct.
"[F]or the duration of the services or any subsequent services" gives the information-sharing consent no fixed end point and "any information" no subject-matter limit.

The cancellation period runs from "the date of the transaction," while the attached Notice of Cancellation measures three days from "the date the contract is signed," and the two dates need not coincide.
The three-day period runs from "the date the contract is signed," whereas the NOTICE in the body of the Agreement runs it from "the date of the transaction."
The promise to return "any payment made by you under this contract" is awkward against the Cost and Payment Terms, under which the CAB fee is not paid up front but financed into the lender's loan.
